about.title: Orinda Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen quickly, but the aftermath can drag on for months. Whether you slipped on a wet floor at a Orinda shopping center off SR-24, tripped on broken pavement in a downtown lot, or fell on poorly lit stairs at an apartment complex, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That's the heart of a premises liability claim here in Contra Costa County. Orinda's mix of hillside properties, older sidewalks, and commercial centers along the SR-24 corridor means hazards can range from drainage issues to uneven walkways. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we connect injured people with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather evidence while it's still available, and explain your options without pressure or upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before It's Too Late

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify evidence, like prior complaints or maintenance logs, that supports this.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make a meaningful difference in how a claim is evaluated.

items.title: Your Deadline May Be Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a premises liability claim, but if a government entity owns or maintains the property, that window shrinks significantly. An attorney can help sort out who's actually responsible.

items.question: I fell at a store near SR-24 in Orinda. What should I do first?
items.answer: Try to document the scene with photos before conditions change, and ask if the location has surveillance cameras covering the area. Report the fall to management and get a copy of any incident report. Then consider speaking with an attorney soon, since evidence like video footage can be lost quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the fall, like not watching where I was walking?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility, though it may reduce the amount. This is a common concern, and it's something an attorney can walk through with you honestly.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after a fall in Orinda?
items.answer: Generally, California allows two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city or county building, that deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim-filing requirement. It's worth checking on this promptly rather than waiting.
